content: 1. Dolasetron and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring is required when these drugs are co-administered. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Donepezil and mefloquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely during co-administration. 3. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of dosulepin by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider using an alternative drug. 4. Mefloquine may enhance the QTc-prolonging effects of agents with a high risk of QTc prolongation. Avoid or use alternative drugs when possible. 5. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of doxepin by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of doxepin cream by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. Additionally, mefloquine increases the toxicity of dronedarone by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 9. Duvelisib increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration increases the AUC of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, potentially increasing the risk of toxicities. Consider reducing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate and monitor for signs of toxicity. 10. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg orally once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended, but close monitoring is advised. 11. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both efavirenz and mefloquine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Elagolix decreases the levels of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A substrate if needed. 13. Eliglustat increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both eliglustat and mefloquine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious or life-threatening events. 15. Encorafenib affects CYP3A4 metabolism and both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Both encorafenib and mefloquine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Entrectinib and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Eribulin and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If concurrent use is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 19. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of mefloquine by prolonging the QTc interval. Mefloquine also increases the toxicity of escitalopram by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Mefloquine increases the levels of esmolol by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the risk of arrhythmia. 22. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Mefloquine increases the levels of everolimus by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Ezogabine and mefloquine both increase the toxicity of each other by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. Monitor the QT interval when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to prolong the QT interval. 25. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of famotidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 27. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of felbamate by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Mefloquine increases the levels of felodipine by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the risk of arrhythmia. 29. Fexinidazole and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 31. Fingolimod and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Increased adverse effects of flibanserin may occur if co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of fluoxetine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. There is potential for increased toxicity. Avoid co-administration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 36. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of foscarnet by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of fosphenytoin by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Mefloquine and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 40. Gemifloxacin and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Gepirone and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Gilteritinib and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Mefloquine and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. If co-administered, obtain ECGs when initiating, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 44. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir also increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Granisetron and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Haloperidol increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both haloperidol and mefloquine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Hydroxyzine and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of ibuprofen/famotidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 51. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of ibutilide by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 52. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 53. Iloperidone increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of iloperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 54. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of imipramine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 55. Indacaterol (inhaled) and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 56. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of indapamide by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 57. Indinavir increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. There is potential for increased toxicity. Avoid co-administration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 58. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of isoflurane by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 60. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Mefloquine increases the levels of isradipine by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mefloquine also increases the toxicity of isradipine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 62. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline at 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 63. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of itraconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 64. Ivacaftor increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite have the potential to inhibit P-gp, which may significantly increase systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 65. Ivosidenib and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of QTc-prolonging drugs with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
